messages:
maria: Quick q — noticed during last peering failover that a bunch of tenant traffic lost source IP preservation. Connector got reallocated and ENI changed. Anyone else hit this?
ash: saw that too last week in staging. flow continuity dropped, app-level retries exploded.
devon: is this eviction from the egress-operator or a control-plane handshake flip? we set lease_ttl pretty low for churn.
maria: digging in — looks like the operator marks connector stale when CP handshakes fail and then reassigns a new connector immediately. so old SNATs gone.
chris: tradeoff: longer connector lease preserves source IP but ties up limited ENIs and increases cost/idle capacity. short TTL reduces wasted IPs but increases churn on failovers.
ine: we prototyped a soft-handoff proxy a while back — old connector stays in a "proxy for existing flows" mode for X minutes after eviction to preserve conntrack. it worked functionally but added complexity to path selections and TLS SNI mapping.
sre-bot: incident 3198765400: connector-eviction-spike detected during us-west peering failover, impacted 12 tenants, elevated to Sev3.
ash: FWIW there's also a routing timing issue — routes for new peering get advertised before old routes are drained, so some traffic flips mid-session. that plus a new ENI -> new IP = broken source preservation.
devon: proposal: make eviction decision depend on data-plane health instead of strictly CP heartbeat. if agent sees active flows / conntrack entries, delay eviction. idle connectors still evict fast.
maria: that seems sensible. question: how to define "active" across AZs and proxies? need threshold to avoid keeping zombie connectors.
chris: heuristic: L4 flow count + recent byte transfer + last packet timestamp. Also a maximum grace window (eg 10m) to bound worst-case idleness.
ine: pseudo policy we used in spike:
```
# egress-operator soft-handoff policy (pseudo)
lease_ttl: 30m
grace_proxy: 10m
evict_if_idle: true
idle_threshold: 2m
max_grace: 10m
```
devon: implementation caveats: conntrack visibility is local to the agent. if flows are proxied through a regional relay, we might not see them. need a tiny flow heartbeat from dataplane to control plane to assert liveliness.
maria: or add a short-lived lease extension protocol: agent can request +1m leases while it sees activity, capped by max_grace. reduces need for global flow visibility.
ash: routing side: don't withdraw old route immediately on new peering activation. prefer a weighted transition (if cloud supports) or a brief overlap with forced client stickiness. prevents flip-flop.
chris: on AWS we can't do BGP weight, but we can delay route removal and instead adjust health-checks so client affinity remains for active sessions. also consider source-based fallback in SNAT table: if primary mapping missing, consult per-tenant fallback map.
ine: soft-handoff + fallback SNAT seems like the least invasive: proxy existing flows while new connector ramps, and if a packet arrives with unknown src we lookup fallback before rewriting. adds a small lookup cost.
sre-bot: FYI recorded metrics we should add: conn_preserve_count, connector_eviction_rate, failed_preserve_count.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: peering-failover-sim at 2026-03-24T20:00Z in canary account. owners: @ine @devon @maria.
devon: I'll run the simulated peering failover tomorrow during the canary window. @ine can you flip soft-handoff flag in canary?
ine: will do. I'll also add the three metrics above and a dashboard.
maria: thanks — let's also add a customer opt-in flag for tenants who need IP stability during cutovers before we roll wide. doc the rollout plan in the playbook.
chris: adding to runbook: steps to revert, how to force immediate eviction if we hit ENI exhaustion, and how to manually drain with migration helper.
nash: one more: validate cross-region latency impact when proxying for grace window. some tenants sensitive to RTT. test with real traffic shapes.
maria: good call. if the canary looks clean we'll iterate on TTL/grace defaults and prepare prod rollout timeline.
ine: opening a tiny RFC PR with the policy + metrics + canary checklist. link when ready.
maria: awesome — thanks all. @chris can you sync with support to draft customer comms for opt-in?
chris: yup will draft and share tomorrow. :thumbsup:
